title: PRD: Hosted endpoints — behavioral edgecases, clarifications, and launch checklist
creator: Amira Patel
summary: This PRD captures a focused set of behavioral clarifications and acceptance criteria for the hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). The goal is to close ambiguous edge cases discovered during integration tests and early partner trials to avoid regressions at launch.
context: Multiple partner integrations surfaced inconsistent behaviors when clients exercised boundary conditions: streaming vs non-streaming partial responses, empty input handling, deterministic tie-breaking in rerank, embedding dimensionality normalization across model variants, and function-calling fallback semantics. These differences cause customer confusion and complicate SDKs and comparators for downstream systems.
goals: Define unambiguous behavioral contracts for each endpoint for edge cases
Provide a prioritized acceptance checklist that gates launch for the hosted surface
Ensure telemetry and test coverage captures these edge cases for post-launch monitoring
Minimize breaking changes for existing customers via graceful compatibility rules
non_goals: Designing new network-level rate limiting policies (ops will follow separate RFC)
Changing core model outputs or training data
Rewriting SDKs end-to-end; SDK patches will be incremental
requirements: REQ-1: Define canonical behavior for empty or whitespace-only prompt inputs for chat and completions
REQ-2: Streaming contract must guarantee that non-terminal 'partial' events are reversible to a final full response without semantic loss
REQ-3: Embeddings endpoint must return explicit 'dimensions' and stable vector normalization across model minor versions
REQ-4: Rerank must document deterministic tie-breaker rules and stable scoring when duplicates or NaNs appear
REQ-5: Function-calling: if function schema mismatch occurs, host must return a structured error with suggested fallback model variant and not silently call an alternate function
REQ-6: When fallback routing (model variant downgrade) occurs due to capacity, response must include a transparent 'served_by' header and a quality-expected delta metric
REQ-7: Rate-limit and burst behavior: documented 429 semantics for batched requests and streaming sessions
REQ-8: Versioning: every response must include model version (semantic tag) and runtime-heuristic flags for known quantization differences
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: End-to-end tests demonstrate deterministic handling of empty prompt for chat and completions: chat returns a system-guided greeting when configured, otherwise 400 with guidance link
AC-2: Streaming smoke tests assert reassembly of partial chunk events into identical final payloads across 1000 sample prompts
AC-3: Embeddings responses include 'dimensions' field and vectors validate length for 99.9% of samples across 3 model variants
AC-4: Rerank tie-breaking reproducible: documented algorithm produces identical ordering for 500 replicated inputs with injected identical scores
AC-5: Function-calling error path returns structured error code and suggested fallback hint; SDK integration test surfaces same structured error
AC-6: Telemetry emits 'fallback_served' metric and 'served_by' header present in 100% of fallback cases during canary
AC-7: Load-testing demonstrates correct 429 behavior for concurrent burst > quota and clients receive idempotency guidance
AC-8: Release notes and API contract docs updated with behavioral edgecases section and example snippets for each case
test_plan: Unit tests: validation for empty inputs, JSON schema validation for function-calling paths
Integration tests: end-to-end across SDKs (node, python, go) asserting headers and body contract
Chaos test: simulate mid-stream connection drop and verify reassembly logic and server-side KV cleanup
Rerank determinism test: synthetic dataset run with seeded RNG to validate deterministic tie-breaking
Embedding normalization test: compare L2 norms across quantized variants and fail if mean delta > 0.02
Canary: 1% traffic routing to canary cluster with telemetry checks for fallback counts, error rates, latency regressions
Manual validation: run partner integration checklist with three early access customers and capture feedback
rollout_checklist: 1) Documentation: Edgecases section added to API reference and snips reviewed by DX
2) SDK patch releases: node@>=2.4.1 python@>=3.8.2 go@>=0.9.5 with handling of new structured errors
3) Telemetry: new metrics instrumented (fallback_served, partial_reassembly_failures, embed_dim_mismatch), dashboards created
4) E2E tests green in release pipeline and canary cluster for 48 hours
5) Support playbook updated with troubleshooting steps and sample cURL commands
6) Release notes drafted with explicit backward-compatibility guarantees and opt-out guidance for experimental flags
7) Ops runbook: capacity thresholds and automated rollback criteria defined
8) Post-launch eval window: 14-day monitoring with weekly review cadence and rapid rollback if quality delta > threshold
metrics: Metric-1: fallback_served_count per model per hour
Metric-5: customer-reported behavioral incidents (SLO: < 2 per 1000 active customers post-launch)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Telemetry under-reporting during canary could hide regressions. Mitigation: Synthetic probes and passive sampling to validate metric pipeline.
Risk: SDK backward incompatibility when surfacing structured errors. Mitigation: Dual-mode error response for two weeks with opt-in header.
Risk: Determinism guarantees may diverge across quantized model builds. Mitigation: Add preflight determinism check in release pipeline and block if divergence > threshold.
Risk: Customers rely on undocumented behavior. Mitigation: Communicate change windows, provide compatibility flags, and offer migration support
notes: This ticket consolidates behavioral clarifications across chat/completions/embeddings/rerank to reduce post-launch incidents. Engineering owners should attach PRs to ENG dependencies. Design/ DX should provide example snippets for each acceptance case. Timeline is tight — prioritize telemetry and docs first to reduce support churn.
